device.name: Network Printer (IPP / AirPrint / IPP Everywhere)
device.notes:
Office and home network printers advertise themselves over mDNS/DNS-SD (Bonjour) using standard, vendor-neutral service types. This project does NOT drive printers: printing is handled by the operating system's print system (AirPrint on Apple platforms, IPP Everywhere / driverless printing elsewhere) or by the vendor's own companion app (HP Smart, Epson Smart Panel, Brother iPrint&Scan, Canon PRINT). We DISCOVER the printer, draw a printer pictogram, and deep-link the user to the printer's embedded web interface so they can manage it.
DNS-SD service types (Bonjour Printing Specification):
  _ipp._tcp             — IPP, the modern print protocol (default TCP 631)
  _ipps._tcp            — IPP over TLS
  _printer._tcp         — legacy LPD (port 515)
  _pdl-datastream._tcp  — raw socket / JetDirect (port 9100)
IPP Everywhere printers additionally advertise the _print._sub._ipps._tcp subtype.
Useful TXT keys: rp (resource path, e.g. "ipp/print"), ty (make-and-model string, good for display), pdl (supported page description languages), UUID (a stable per-printer identifier — IPP Everywhere printers advertise one), adminurl (the printer's own admin page, when published), note (location) and product. The display name comes from the mDNS instance name (ty is a good fallback); the stable key is the TXT UUID, falling back to the hostname.
admin_url defaults to http://<ip>/ because most printers serve an embedded web server at the root. A printer that advertises TXT adminurl supplies a more exact link and a consumer should prefer it. Scheme/port may be reconfigured (many printers redirect the root to https).

credentials.notes: Identify-only: no credential crosses to this app. Any printer admin password is entered by the user at the printer's own web UI, which we only deep-link to.

factory_reset.effect: Not this project's concern: a printer's factory reset is done at the device and clears the printer's own settings, not anything this app stores. We only identify the printer.

methods.description: No provisioning is performed by this app. The printer joins the network by its own setup (WPS, vendor app, or wired), after which it is discovered passively by its _ipp._tcp / _ipps._tcp advertisement.

setup.notes: Nothing for this app to provision: the printer is already on the LAN and advertises itself over mDNS. We browse for the standard IPP service types, read the TXT record, draw the printer pictogram and offer the embedded-web-server link. The printer is set up (and printed to) through the OS print system or the vendor's own app, not here.

rejoin.notes: The printer stays discoverable by its DNS-SD advertisement wherever it sits on the LAN; identity keys on the TXT UUID (or hostname), not IP, so a DHCP move does not lose it.

testing.notes: No hardware exercised by this project. The discovery signature here is taken from public standards — Apple's Bonjour Printing Specification and the PWG/IETF IPP + IPP Everywhere documents — not from a capture of a specific printer. The service types (_ipp._tcp, _ipps._tcp, _printer._tcp, _pdl-datastream._tcp) and the TXT keys are vendor-neutral and standardised, so identification rests on the standard itself rather than any one model.

local_access.summary: Printers are natively usable locally through the OS print system (AirPrint / IPP Everywhere driverless printing) with no vendor cloud — this project deliberately scopes the entry to identify-only and hands the user to the printer's embedded web interface for management.
